instructions:
peek: See what your agents made, wherever you are. It keeps the images, videos and audio you make, on this host, and gives each a link that shows or plays it in the person's browser, on their phone too. Upload a screenshot, a screen recording or a sound you want the person to see or hear, and give them its link (in a PR, a task comment or a message) instead of attaching the file.

- upload_asset takes the file's name and what it is for: repo (owner/name) and pr, task (a waypoint short id), title, tags. Give content (the file in base64) only for a small file, up to a few MB. For anything larger, give no content: it answers an uploadUrl and the exact curl command to run in your shell, which needs no token and works once, within the hour. Either way it answers the asset's link.
- Give the person link, never fileUrl: link is the page that plays it.
- list_assets finds what was uploaded, newest first, by repo, pr, task, tags, contentType prefix (video/), createdBy or text in q; pass nextToken for the next page.
- update_asset changes what an asset is of; delete_asset removes it and its file.
- Every tool takes the token this server was connected with.

tools.name: upload_asset
tools.title: Upload an asset
tools.description: Keeps a file and answers its `link`, the page that shows or plays it, to give the person. With `content` (base64, for a small file) it is stored now and the asset answered. Without it, answers an `uploadUrl` and the `curl` command that uploads the file from your shell: run it with `<file>` replaced by the file's path. It needs no token, works once within the hour, and answers the asset; the `link` answered now works once it has run.

name.description: The file's name, with its extension: no path.

contentType.description: Its media type, such as `video/mp4`. Default: the name's extension's.

title.description: What it shows, in a few words.

description.description: More on what it shows, or what to look for.

repo.description: The GitHub repository it is for, as `owner/name`.

pr.description: The pull request it is for, in `repo`.

task.description: The waypoint task it is for, by its short id.

items.description: A tag: any text without a comma.

content.description: The file, in base64, for a small one (at most 16,000,000 characters, about 12 MB). Leave it out to be given an uploadUrl and a curl command that uploads the file from your shell instead.

tools.name: list_assets
tools.title: List assets
tools.description: Assets matching every filter given, newest first, a page at a time: while `nextToken` is not null, pass it for the next page.

pr.description: Only those for this pull request.

task.description: Only those for this waypoint task.

tags.description: Only those carrying every one of these tags.

contentType.description: Only those whose media type starts with this, such as `video/` or `image/png`.

createdBy.description: Only those uploaded by this caller.

q.description: Only those whose name, title or description holds this text, ignoring case.

nextToken.description: The `nextToken` a page answered, for the page after it.

tools.name: update_asset
tools.title: Update an asset
tools.description: Sets what an asset is of: the fields given, leaving the rest. Its bytes and name do not change.

title.description: What it shows, in a few words; null clears it.

description.description: More on what it shows; null clears it.

anyOf.description: More on what it shows, or what to look for.

repo.description: The repository it is for, as `owner/name`; null clears it.

pr.description: The pull request it is for; null clears it.

task.description: The waypoint task it is for; null clears it.

tags.description: Its tags, replacing those it had.

items.description: A tag: any text without a comma.

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.title: Delete an asset
tools.description: Removes the asset from the catalog, then its file. Its link and file URL answer 404 after.
